agree.reason: The email apologises plainly, names the exact failure this household felt (no credit, silence), and makes concrete commitments, so a hurt but persuadable member is likely to reconsider; it offers nothing for last year's lost value, which may still hold back the most resentful readers.

honest.reason: Every fact matches the brief and what the user said, and the limits are stated (the nets don't cover greens, no guarantee against loss), though 'you'll always know what's happening' promises a little more than one short weekly email can deliver.

works_the_facts.reason: The facts are passed along as given, with nothing worked out from them: no '29 of 41' instead of the vague 'most of you', no dollar value of a weekly credit (about $24.50), and no estimate of what the six thin weeks cost a member.

right_comparison.reason: Last season's handling is contrasted clearly with this season's policies at the same price, but the email never describes what the reader gets if they stay away, and it doesn't say that only 52 shares are left against 97 departures.

qualification.reason: The 'more than a third' credit threshold and the weekly Thursday email are specific commitments the reader can check, but the email doesn't say who decides a box was cut by a third or how the credit is paid.

objections.reason: It meets the 'you went quiet' objection directly with the weekly-email commitment and the credit policy, without raising doubts the facts already answer, though it leaves unspoken whether last year's losses will ever be made good.

fit.reason: It is a well-formed email whose body comes to about 200 words, landing right at the limit and slightly over once the subject line is counted.
